title: Apple Warns Users in 110 Countries of Mercenary Spyware Attacks
excerpt: The tech giant's latest threat notification wave alerts journalists, activists, and diplomats worldwide, urging them to enable Lockdown Mode immediately.
body:
• Apple has sent threat notifications to iPhone users in 110 countries warning of sophisticated mercenary spyware attacks targeting specific individuals.
  • The company recommends immediately enabling Lockdown Mode and directs affected users to nonprofit Access Now for digital security support.
  • India is among the countries affected, with previous waves reaching journalists, opposition politicians, and activists.

Apple has dispatched a fresh wave of threat notifications to iPhone users across 110 countries, warning them that their devices may have been individually targeted by mercenary spyware — the most sophisticated and expensive class of digital surveillance tools in existence.

The notifications, sent via iMessage, email, and a banner on Apple's account page, mark the latest round in a program the company launched in November 2021. Apple has now alerted users in more than 150 countries since the program began, sending notifications multiple times per year as it detects new attack campaigns.

What the Notifications Say

"Apple detected that you are being targeted by a mercenary spyware attack that is trying to remotely compromise the iPhone associated with your Apple Account," the notification reads, according to recipients who have shared the message publicly. "This attack is likely targeting you specifically because of who you are or what you do."

https://x.com/PortalCripto/status/2088071721614016520

The company urges recipients to take the warning seriously, noting that while absolute certainty is never possible, Apple has "high confidence" in the alerts. It recommends enabling Lockdown Mode — a feature that restricts device functionality to block sophisticated attack vectors — and directs users to Access Now, a nonprofit that operates a round-the-clock digital security helpline for journalists, activists, and civil society members.

Who Gets Targeted

Mercenary spyware attacks differ fundamentally from ordinary cybercrime. They cost millions of dollars per deployment, exploit zero-day vulnerabilities, and target a very small number of specific individuals. The primary targets are journalists, political activists, politicians, diplomats, and human rights defenders.

Apple's support page specifically names NSO Group and its Pegasus spyware as an example of the commercial surveillance tools involved, though the company does not attribute individual notifications to specific attackers or governments.

"Mercenary spyware attacks, such as those using Pegasus from the NSO Group, are exceptionally rare and vastly more sophisticated than regular cybercriminal activity or consumer malware."

— Apple threat notification

India Among Affected Countries

India has featured prominently in previous notification waves. In October 2023, Apple alerts sent to several Indian opposition politicians and journalists triggered a political firestorm, with recipients including members of parliament and newsroom editors. The Indian government at the time questioned the accuracy of Apple's detection methods, though independent forensic analyses by organizations like Citizen Lab and Amnesty International have repeatedly confirmed Pegasus infections on devices of Indian journalists and activists.

The latest round of notifications arrives as governments worldwide continue to grapple with the commercial spyware industry. A coalition of countries including the United States has been working to develop safeguards against the abuse of surveillance technology, while the European Parliament has investigated member states' use of Pegasus and similar tools.

What Users Should Do

Apple advises anyone who receives a threat notification to enable Lockdown Mode immediately under Settings > Privacy & Security, update their device to the latest iOS version, and contact Access Now's Digital Security Helpline for specialized assistance. The company also recommends updating all other Apple devices and messaging apps.

For the vast majority of iPhone users, mercenary spyware remains a remote threat. Apple emphasizes that these attacks target an extremely small number of individuals and that most users will never receive a threat notification. But for those who do, the company's message is unambiguous: take it seriously.
